status_summary: A DOL Secretary's memorandum of 2025-06-23, as reported by a law firm, created a temporary Office of Immigration Policy within the Office of the Secretary, led by the OFLC administrator, which monitors foreign labor certification in consultation with ETA. DOL's FY2027 Budget in Brief proposes making OFLC an independent DOL agency separate from ETA, with $86.8 million requested within the Departmental Management appropriation; a law-firm report of 2026-04-13 says it would report to the Deputy Secretary. The House Appropriations Committee reported H.R. 9260 (Report 119-696) on 2026-06-11 with foreign labor certification funded in the ETA account, and no enacted appropriation or order moving OFLC out of ETA was found.

timeline.event: A Secretary's memorandum created a temporary Office of Immigration Policy within the Office of the Secretary, focused on employment-based visas and led by the OFLC administrator, with a duty to work with the ETA Assistant Secretary on foreign labor certification policy.

The House Appropriations Committee reported H.R. 9260 (Report 119-696), which funds foreign labor certification within the Employment and Training Administration account and does not mention an independent OFLC.

title: Move OFLC out of ETA under a politically accountable director
uncertainties: The FY2027 Budget in Brief was read on dol.gov on 2026-10-18; it prints no publication date and does not state a reporting line, and its page 33 places the $23.3 million state grant portion in the State Grants appropriation, slightly inconsistent with page 14. The Deputy Secretary reporting line comes from a law-firm report dated 2026-04-13. The Secretary's 2025-06-23 memorandum was not opened; its date and terms come from a law-firm article. The reported House text of H.R. 9260 was read on govinfo.gov in two parts; it funds foreign labor certification at $87,810,000 in the ETA State Unemployment Insurance and Employment Service Operations account and does not mention an independent OFLC. House Report 119-696 pages 33 to 34 (Departmental Management) were not read. Senate action and the final FY2027 appropriation were not checked; congress.gov could not be opened. A Federal Register API query found no OFLC reorganization notice since 2025-06-01.
